name: litebox
description: A security-focused library OS supporting kernel- and user-mode execution
readmeExcerpt:
# LiteBox

> A security-focused library OS

> [!NOTE]  
> This project is currently actively evolving and improving. While we are
> working toward a stable release, some APIs and interfaces may change as the
> design continues to mature. You are welcome to explore and experiment, but if
> you need long-term stability, it may be best to wait for a stable release, or
> be prepared to adapt to updates along the way.

LiteBox is a sandboxing library OS that drastically cuts down the interface to the host, thereby reducing attack surface.  It focuses on easy interop of various "North" shims and "South" platforms.  LiteBox is designed for usage in both kernel and non-kernel scenarios.

LiteBox exposes a Rust-y [`nix`](https://docs.rs/nix)/[`rustix`](https://docs.rs/rustix)-inspired "North" interface when it is provided a `Platform` interface at its "South".  These interfaces allow for a wide variety of use-cases, easily allowing for connection between any of the North--South pairs.

Example use cases include:
- Running unmodified Linux programs on Windows
- Sandboxing Linux applications on Linux
- Run programs on top of SEV SNP
- Running OP-TEE programs on Linux
- Running on LVBS



## Contributing

aiSummary.oneLiner: A lightweight sandbox from Microsoft for securely running untrusted code.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Litebox is a minimal, highly secure sandboxing environment engineered by Microsoft to execute unverified or untrusted code safely. It creates a strict boundary around the execution context, preventing malicious scripts from accessing the host's filesystem, network, or other sensitive system resources. Designed to be significantly faster and lighter than traditional virtual machines, it allows for high-performance code execution with very low overhead. The project is an ideal building block for platforms that require rapid, secure code evaluation, such as automated testing suites or AI agent playgrounds.
keyFeatures: Strict Isolation: Enforces rigid boundaries to ensure untrusted code absolutely cannot access host system resources.
Minimal Overhead: Designed to launch rapidly and consume a fraction of the memory required by traditional VMs.
Secure Execution Constraints: Actively blocks unauthorized filesystem writes, network exfiltration, and malicious system calls.
High-Performance Architecture: Optimized to execute code efficiently without the heavy virtualization penalties of full-stack hypervisors.
Embeddable Design: Structured to be easily integrated into larger platforms like CI/CD pipelines or AI evaluation systems.

useCases.title: AI Code Evaluation
useCases.description: AI development platforms integrate Litebox to safely execute, test, and score code generated autonomously by large language models.

useCases.title: Automated Code Testing
useCases.description: CI/CD pipelines utilize the sandbox to securely run automated test suites against user-submitted, potentially dangerous pull requests.

useCases.title: Secure Coding Playgrounds
useCases.description: Educational platforms deploy it to provide users with fast, interactive, and completely safe in-browser coding environments.

useCases.title: Malware Analysis
useCases.description: Security researchers execute suspicious scripts within the isolated environment to safely monitor their behavior without risking the host system.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Litebox is built for security engineers, system administrators, and developers building platforms that execute arbitrary code. Users must possess a strong understanding of system security, sandboxing concepts, and integration APIs.
